protocol: Filing-level attribution of insurer disclosures to a named hurricane
reference_unit: One economically labelled USD measure in one filing for the selected event. Repeated mentions in the same filing count once. A later filing counts as a new disclosure. Separately named measures with coincident amounts remain separate when the source supplies a distinct label or accounting concept. Forecasts, payments, reserves and individual components are distinct. All positive and negative cases within the selected primary forms are retained.
automatic: Only final emitted rows marked automatic count; holds, unscored diagnostic facts and candidates for review earn no automatic credit. Historical extractors are evaluated exactly as run; no manual repair or multiplication of amounts by reviewers.
amount_event_match: Same filing, target event, exact source-normalized dollar endpoints and open/closed bound, and evidence identifying the same monetary assertion. An identical amount read in a different claim, date, row, or unallocated combined-storm figure does not match. Approximate rounded amounts can match the source's own reported precision only. A reference can be credited only once. If a repeated number is compatible with two measures, a specific table column or economic label must resolve the match, and one row may never earn two credits.
full_semantic_match: In addition to amount and event, the structured output must identify the affected entity or segment, meaningful metric and economic basis (such as gross, retained or ceded where stated), accounting status, and as-stated period/as-of date. A filing acceptance date cannot supply the economic period. A table statement must give enough evidence to locate its measure, current-year column and scale. For operating segments with only contextual post-cession basis, the correct reported segment expense label with contextual/unspecified basis is acceptable; an unsupported explicit gross/net label is not. A tax qualifier, direction, scope, bound or timing that contradicts the source bars full credit. For repeated rows score unique matches and also report contradictions separately. Do not silently use neighboring figures to repair a prediction.
precision_accounting: Enumerate every automatic output. Classify it as supported amount-event, unsupported/contradicted amount-event, or unavoidable ambiguity (counts as unsupported in precision). Count supported duplicates separately from unique hits. If a correct numeric row has wrong entity or accounting kind, record the semantic failure separately. Report counts of automatic rows, unsupported rows, reviews and exact duplicate rows. Calculate distinct reference coverage, full-semantic coverage and supported-row fraction separately. A zero gold denominator yields undefined recall; a zero output denominator yields undefined precision.
baseline: Use the frozen HCI source reference and the published v3 output. For the new issuer run both frozen methods on the identically selected inputs under the identical scoring rules. Financial rows with an exchange rate, policy limits, other events, market-wide reference or unallocated package do not receive named-event attribution.
holdout: Selected by the collection agent before reading the contents, the new issuer's source-first reference is closed independently of test predictions. The developer cannot see its inputs or labels until v4 is locked. Local times and digests document sequencing; this is an internal evaluation, not a registered or externally validated benchmark.
disagreement: List each genuine economic-definition ambiguity and provide a sensitivity denominator where appropriate. Missing source rows or factual errors in a reference may be corrected through the original filing with a written change log, preserving its original hash and scores where applicable. Never change the target because an extractor scored poorly.
